status: EXPLORATORY: MIST isochrones fitted to Gaia colour-magnitude diagrams and the stellar masses read off them

source.name: MIST v1.2 (MESA Isochrones and Stellar Tracks), rotating models v/vcrit = 0.4, synthetic photometry UBV(RI)c + 2MASS + Kepler + Hipparcos + Tycho + Gaia
cite: Choi et al. 2016, ApJ 823, 102 (MIST I: the models)
Paxton et al. 2011, ApJS 192, 3 and later MESA instrument papers
source.note: The tarball's .iso.cmd files carry Gaia EDR3 passbands (Gaia_G_EDR3, Gaia_BP_EDR3, Gaia_RP_EDR3), which Gaia DR3 photometry shares, beside the older DR2 and MAW ones; SDP reads the EDR3 columns. Header and columns checked against the real tarball on 2026-11-15.

extinction.note: A_X / A_V for the Gaia bands, Wang and Chen 2019, ApJ 877, 116; one ratio per band, so a colour-dependent extinction is not modelled

parallax.note: Gaia EDR3/DR3 parallaxes read about 0.017 mas too small (Lindegren et al. 2021, A&A 649, A4); a cluster's mean parallax also carries about 0.01 mas of correlated error on degree scales

photometry.note: the bulk Gaia copy has no photometric errors, so a smooth model of them by G; the floors stand for the models' own uncertainty, the DR2/DR3 passband difference and unresolved binaries

metallicity_prior.note: A Gaussian prior on the fitted [Fe/H]: the first PC runs (2026-11-16) showed a Gaia CMD of 20 to 150 stars barely fixes metallicity (it trades against dust; red-dwarf colours and the horizontal branch pull fits to the grid's ends: 43 of 112 fits at -2.5 or +0.5). Known clusters take their spectroscopic [Fe/H] (Harris 1996, 2010 edition, for the globulars; alpha_fe 0.3 for globulars), others the disc's radial gradient within z_max_kpc of the plane (about -0.07 dex/kpc, e.g. Myers et al. 2022, AJ 164, 85), the halo beyond. NOT YET VERIFIED: the numbers were entered from memory; Leigh to check them against Harris 2010 and the gradient paper.

field_stars.note: one star with no cluster: weights over every grid point of one metallicity, a Kroupa (2001) initial mass function and a prior uniform in age, so its age is usually poorly fixed and its mass is fixed far better

known_answers.note: Broad sanity windows, NOT binding: Leigh to check each against a published Gaia isochrone fit (for example Gaia Collaboration, Babusiaux et al. 2018, A&A 616, A10) before they become a check that fails the run. The globulars (M5, M3, M30) are about 11 to 13 Gyr old with [Fe/H] near -1.3, -1.5 and -2.3 (Harris 1996, 2010 edition); their [Fe/H] windows reach 0.2 dex above that because MIST's solar-scaled models stand in for alpha-enhanced stars
